title: LLM-Pilot: Characterize and Optimize Performance of your LLM Inference Services
problem: Understanding which hardware will deliver required performance for LLM inference services serving thousands of concurrent users while satisfying performance requirements remains challenging. Selecting optimal hardware configuration for a given LLM and performance target requires extensive, costly benchmarking.
motivation: LLMs are rapidly growing in popularity and organizations need practical methods to deploy inference services cost-effectively while meeting performance SLOs.
method: LLM-Pilot benchmarks LLM inference services under realistic workloads across various GPUs and optimizes service configuration for each GPU to maximize performance. It learns a predictive model from characterization data to recommend cost-effective hardware for previously unseen LLMs without full re-benchmarking, using the learned model to guide hardware selection decisions.
key_novelty: Using systematic hardware characterization and machine learning to predict optimal hardware and service configuration for LLM inference before deployment, enabling cost-effective hardware selection without exhaustive benchmarking.
contributions: LLM-Pilot system for characterizing and predicting LLM inference service performance
Benchmarking methodology across diverse GPUs under realistic workloads
Configuration optimization techniques per GPU to maximize performance
Predictive model for recommending cost-effective hardware for new LLMs
primary_theme: Hardware characterization and optimization for LLM inference
